messages:
oliver: AcmePay seeing intermittent Go SDK stream failures. Error printed: \"scanner: unexpected token boundary\". Repro on Go SDK v0.9.2. Anyone seen this before?

raj: Can you paste logs + a minimal repro? Is this streaming Chat or completions?

oliver: Streaming chat. Log snippet below — looks like JSON fragments split across reads.

```
2026-03-15T15:12:02Z stream recv: \"data: {\\\"choices\\\":[{\\\"delta\\\":{\\\"content\\\":\\\"Hel\"}}]}

\"
2026-03-15T15:12:02Z stream recv: \"lo\\\"}}]}

\"
2026-03-15T15:12:02Z scanner error: unexpected EOF in JSON token
```

jen: Are you using bufio.Scanner defaults? Scanner has token size limits and splits. Which Go and SDK versions?

oliver: Go 1.20, Redwood Go SDK v0.9.2. Minimal snippet: 

```
resp, _ := client.Stream(ctx, req)
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body)
for scanner.Scan() {
  fmt.Println(scanner.Text())
}
```

Looks like scanner splits mid-SSE event or mid-JSON; stream uses SSE-like `data: ` prefixes.

emily: Right — bufio.Scanner is line-oriented and has limits. Also note our server sends SSE-esque frames so chunking can split lines. json.Decoder won't work because of the `data: ` prefix lines. You need to aggregate until the SSE event delimiter (`\n\n`).

oliver: I tried increasing scanner.Buffer(...), still intermittent. Error rate ~1%. Happens after ~20-200 tokens.

raj: Could also be proxy/nginx chunking — Transfer-Encoding: chunked divides bytes arbitrarily. I can reproduce locally by randomly splitting writes.

oliver: Suspect our SDK stream parser merges incoming reads incorrectly when a partial `data:` line and next read contains rest; mutex/race or concat logic might drop separators.

jen: Can you share the request id + trace so I can escalate to eng-runtime?

oliver: req-id: rdx-1234-zz. Trace: https://console.redwood/trace/rdx-1234-zz (internal). Repro steps:
1) Run minimal Go app with SDK v0.9.2
2) Start chat stream with conversation >200 tokens
3) Observe intermittent scanner errors ~1/100 connections

Minimal repro snippet I used:
```
client.Config.Token = os.Getenv("REDWOOD_TOKEN")
req := &openai.ChatStreamRequest{ /* long prompt */ }
stream, _ := client.Chat.Stream(ctx, req)
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(stream.Body)
scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 4096), 1024*1024)
for scanner.Scan() { log.Println(scanner.Text()) }
```

raj: I wrote a small local harness that injects random byte splits and I can reproduce the malformed JSON when the parser assumes each `scanner.Text()` is a full SSE event. Fix: accumulate bytes until `\n\n` event delimiter then process the event body, strip `data: ` prefixes, and decode.

emily: Workaround for customers: use a custom reader that collects until `\n\n` instead of Scanner, then strip the `data: ` prefix and json.Unmarshal. Example pattern:

```
buf := make([]byte, 0)
r := stream.Body
b := make([]byte, 4096)
for {
  n, err := r.Read(b)
  if n > 0 { buf = append(buf, b[:n]...) }
  for {
    idx := bytes.Index(buf, []byte("\n\n"))
    if idx < 0 { break }
    evt := buf[:idx]
    // strip 'data: ' lines, merge, decode, emit
    buf = buf[idx+2:]
  }
  if err != nil { break }
}
```

jen: :thumbsup: I'll open an internal ticket to add a resilient SSE parser to the Go SDK and schedule a patch. For immediate mitigation recommend customers either: 1) use the wrapper above, 2) upgrade to 0.10.0-alpha (nightly) where we added partial fixes, or 3) pin scanner.Buffer to a large capacity plus event-aggregation.

go-support-bot: Support ticket #SUP-2026 created and assigned to eng-runtime. ETA for triage: 2 business days.

oliver: Thanks — customer is impacted (billing account set). Please ping when a release is available.

emily: Adding a regression test that simulates random chunk splits and SSE framing. Will post PR link when ready.
